messages:
tess (pm): quick sync: we need to decide how multi-controller onprem installs handle concurrent abort/rollback commands. split-brain and duplicate leader actions are my main worry. any lightweight model we can adopt?

ian (eng-arch): good call. two obvious options: 1) central sequencer (single leader) that linearizes ledger writes, or 2) CRDT-style merge for ledger entries with tombstone semantics. sequencer is simpler but needs strong leader election and failover guarantees.

rohit (eng-infra): sequencer + monotonic seq per-manifest seems easiest for audits. controllers can elect leader via etcd, and leader signs ledger entries. followers proxy operator actions to leader. downside: leader becomes a hot path for large fleets.

sasha (controller): operational nuance: many of our private installs run multiple controllers for HA. if leader is down we still want operators to be able to issue a local "quarantine" quickly. propose local-stub entries with sig_type=local_provisional that later get reconciled/confirmed by leader.

morgan (operator): +1 to local provisional. real-world: when cluster controller OOMs, waiting for leader election kills time. operators need a fast guardrail to stop serving. but how reconcile when two locals try to abort same shard?

ian (eng-arch): reconciliation rules: provisional entries are accepted temporarily by installers if they include proof (signed by local operator key) and must be given a TTL. leader reconciliation picks the highest-seq or earliest-authoritative entry and appends a confirming ledger entry. provisional entries become authoritative only after leader confirmation or after a configurable timeout they get auto-rolled back.

anya (security): security constraints: provisional signatures must be auditable and include operator key id + attestation blob (e.g., controller cert fingerprint). ledger must record sig_provenance and provisional=true. Only leader-signed entries can move shard to COMMITTED. Anything else is non-authoritative.

rohit (eng-infra): implement flow idea: 1) operator hits fast-abort on a local controller, 2) controller writes provisional ledger CBOR to local store with TTL and emits invalidate token signed with local key, 3) controller forwards action to elected leader; leader either confirms (writes leader-signed ledger entry) or writes an explicit NACK.

sasha (controller): exact token semantics: provisional tokens should be marked `token_type=provisional` and include `controller_id` and `provisional_ttl`. serving nodes must accept provisional invalidates but restrict their blast radius: provisional invalidation will mark prefixes as quarantined but will not delete persisted caches until leader confirms. that keeps serving consistent under reconciliation.

morgan (operator): so serving nodes have two layers: soft-quarantine (from provisional) and hard-evict (from leader commit). perfect. need UI flags so oncall knows a provisional action is in-flight.

tess (pm): UX: console should show provisional actions in orange with a "confirm" column pointing to leader seq when confirmed. also surface which controller issued provisional action.

ian (eng-arch): data model: ledger entry fields (flat string example in RFC):
```
seq: "1024"
manifest: "m-2026-07-01"
shard: "sh-A7"
state: "PROVISIONAL_QUARANTINE"
actor: "operator:morgan@controller-s1"
sig_type: "local"
sig_provenance: "controller-cert:fingerprint"
ts: "1839990000"
provisional_ttl: "30s"
```
Leader confirmation appends: `seq:1025 state:CONFIRMED_QUARANTINE leader:controller-s2 sig_type:kms`

anya (security): also include `nonce` and `prev_seq` in provisional entries to avoid accidental forks. leader reconciliation must preserve ordering by `prev_seq` where possible and flag conflicts for human review.

rohit (eng-infra): conflict resolution policy idea: if two provisional actions target the same shard, leader picks winner by earliest ts unless there's a higher-authority signature. we record conflict in ledger with `conflict=[seqA,seqB]` so auditors can trace.

sasha (controller): additional implementation detail: controllers replicate ledger entries to local compacted WAL so restarts don't lose provisional entries. leader confirmation can prune provisional copies and coalesce.

morgan (operator): CLI needs to show provisional -> confirmed transitions. example: `redwoodctl activation status --manifest m-2026-07-01 --shard sh-A7` should show both: latest_provisional_seq and leader_confirmed_seq.

ian (eng-arch): serving-plane contract change: serveable state machine now considers soft-quarantine for provisional tokens (no hard eviction). once leader confirms, serving performs hard-evict and publishes ack. a node that processed provisional invalidation must accept a later leader confirm without race issues. include idempotency keys.

anya (security): cryptography notes: local provisional signatures should use local controller keypair stored in HSM when available. include `sig_chain` if controller used an operator-signed temporary certificate. ledger entries must include `sig_key_id` and `sig_chain` strings.

rohit (eng-infra): metrics to add: provisional_actions_count, provisional_confirm_rate, provisional_conflict_rate, leader_confirmation_latency. SRE can alert if confirmation latency > threshold.

tess (pm): runbook update: when provisional remains unconfirmed > TTL, controllers either auto-retry forward-to-leader or escalate to human intervention. include steps to surface provisional tombstones in console and run `redwoodctl activation reconcile --manifest m-...` to force leader reconciliation if needed.

sasha (controller): we'll add a reconciliation endpoint on leader that returns unresolved provisional entries and provides an API to confirm/resolve. also will provide `--force` bypass for emergency ops (audit flagged).

morgan (operator): emergency ops: allow `redwoodctl activation confirm --provisional-seq 204 --reason \"emergency\" --force` but require additional approver signature (2nd operator) for audit.

ian (eng-arch): ok action items for RFC patch: 1) multi-controller provisional model + reconciliation algorithm (ian+sasha) 2) ledger schema additions: provisional fields + conflict records (ian+anya) 3) console/cli UX for provisional visibility and reconcilers (tess+morgan+leah) 4) serving-plane semantics for soft vs hard invalidation (ian+rohit) 5) metrics and alerts (rohit) 6) runbook changes + emergency confirm flow (morgan).

ops-bot: reminder: add integration test that simulates leader failover during provisional abort.

tess (pm): thanks all. i'll fold this into RFC follow-up and try to PR by EOD Friday. any objections?

ian (eng-arch): no objections. this covers split-brain risk reasonably.

anya (security): one last note: ensure archived provisional entries are preserved in immutable archive as well so compliance can reconstruct events even if provisional was never confirmed.

morgan (operator): noted. thanks team.
